decisions.reason: The firm has already publicly committed this specialized particle-therapy phantom with a stated release timetable, and in this escalation-of-commitment setting management is likely to give it more time despite its narrower niche and delayed US availability.

As a newly launched ionization chamber squarely within the firm's core dosimetry business and visibly promoted on its own page, it is likely to be retained while management seeks to justify the launch and build adoption.

Although another small-volume chamber may create some overlap in the range, the public launch and fit with the firm's established measurement portfolio make management more likely to persist than to withdraw it quickly.

A standard clinical ionization chamber is highly aligned with the firm's long-standing capabilities, customer base, and service model, so management would be very reluctant to write off the investment after launch.

This relative-dosimetry chamber supports the firm's core QA offering and customer workflow, and with no clear sign of failure management would likely continue backing it rather than admit an early mistake.

A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, complementary product for the firm's established market, so the combination of sunk development effort and public commitment makes near-term withdrawal unlikely.
